title: Low-degree cohomology of a right derived functor sees only low degrees
statement: Let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive] between Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], with right derived functor $Rv:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ computed by K-injective resolutions [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Let $n\in\mathbf Z$ and let $c:L\to M$ be a morphism of $D^+(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] such that $\mathcal H^i(c):\mathcal H^i(L)\to\mathcal H^i(M)$ (cohomology functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]) is an isomorphism for every $i\leq n$ and a monomorphism for $i=n+1$. Then $\mathcal H^j(Rv(c)):\mathcal H^j(RvL)\to\mathcal H^j(RvM)$ is an isomorphism for every $j\leq n$. In particular, for $K\in D^+(\mathcal A)$ and the canonical truncation $c_n:\tau_{\leq n}K\to K$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] (of a bounded below complex representing $K$), the map $\mathcal H^n(Rv\,\tau_{\leq n}K)\to\mathcal H^n(RvK)$ induced by $c_n$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: **Step 1 (general map theorem).** The isomorphism conclusion for the right derived functor follows by applying the separately stated monomorphism and epimorphism halves degreewise and using that a morphism in an abelian category which is both monic and epic is an isomorphism.

**Step 2 (canonical truncation).** Apply `DerivedCategory.Plus.isIso_homologyFunctor_map_map_truncLEι_app` to `v.rightDerivedFunctorPlus`. Its lower-degree vanishing hypothesis is exactly `v.isZero_homologyFunctor_rightDerivedFunctorPlus_obj_of_isGE`, the negative-vanishing theorem, instantiated with the truncation lower bound and the requested degree. This directly proves the degree-`n` cohomology map for the canonical lower truncation.
